title: MBALA CBD GETS FACELIFT THROUGH THE PRESIDENT AVENUE CDF PROJECT
text_content: Mbala District is bustling with excitement as the President Avenue Constituency Development Fund project is underway, promising to enhance the infrastructure and aesthetics of the Central Business District. Funded under the 2025 CDF allocation at a cost of 8.7 million kwacha, this high value project focuses on a critical 2.5 kilometer stretch of Mbala’s main street, aiming to improve urban infrastructure. The scope of the project includes construction of a high capacity Drainage System, Paving of Walkways and Installation of Street Lights. These enhancements are set to provide a safer and more accessible highway for pedestrians, cyclists and motorists. Currently, the contractor has made substantial progress in excavating the drainage and is actively paving the Sidewalks and installing Curb Stones along the designated stretch, representing 30% progress on the project. This project is crucial in improving overall road safety, reducing flooding risks and assuring longevity of President Avenue. Additionally, the project has created temporary employment opportunities for 48 local residents, which has improved their livelihoods and facilitated community involvement in the development process, ensuring that the benefits of the project extend beyond infrastructure improvements.

title: CDF WATER BOWSER DELIVERED TO MBALA DISTRICT
text_content: Mbala Municipal Council has successfully procured a brand new Shacman Water Bowser, procured at a cost of K2,200,000.00 under the 2026 Constituency Development Fund (CDF) allocation. The Machinery is a versatile asset with a capacity of 20,000 Litres, equipped with an inbuilt water pump for efficient operation. The equipment was supplied by Higer Bus Zambia Limited, who also conducted an orientation training to ensure that operators at the Local Authority are well equipped to operate the machine, thus guaranteeing effective utilization and maintenance of the equipment. Mbala Municipal Council Town Clerk Mrs. Laura Yumba Munkanta stated as she received the equipment at the Civic Centre, on 22nd June 2026, that acquisition of the Water Bowser will ensure supply of water for grading, compacting and dust suppression during feeder road developments. In addition to the water bowser, the Council is expecting the arrival of a Shacman Low Bed Trailer and a CAT Bulldozer in the coming weeks. The Council previously procured a Grader, Tipper Truck and a Tractor Loader Backhoe which have been utilized to open up and rehabilitate various feeder roads in the District including Kawimbe – Itokoto road, Kamba – Kakungu – Isofu road, Kaseshya – Itokoto and Chipoma – Chalamanga roads. The Council has also rehabilitated various township feeder roads.

title: Mandate – Mbala Municipal Council
text_content: Mandate – Mbala Municipal Council Menu Our Mandate Functions of Local Authorities (Councils) The Council derives its mandate from the Local Government Act which lists the following as overall functions of Local Authorities: • Maintain law and order and effective administration of Local Authorities to ensure national security; • Control the keeping and movement of livestock, slaughtering of animals, sale of meat and enforce the disposal of diseased animals carcasses or meat which is unfit for human consumption; • Take measures for storage, market and preservation of agricultural produce and prevention of agricultural produce, conservation of natural resources and prevention of soil erosion; • Control the manufacture, storage, sale and use of petroleum, fireworks gas and other combustible or dangerous substance; • Construct and maintain public roads, streets, sanitary lanes, bridges and water courses and remove all obstacles thereof; • Establish and maintain sanitation and drainage systems to facilitate the removal of refuse and effluent; • Provide for the registration of births, marriage, deaths, clubs and enumeration of persons or property connected with the administration of Council areas; • Establish and maintain colleges, schools and day nurseries; • Prepare and administer schemes for community participation in development; • Establish and maintain a system of street lighting and in public places; • Establish and maintain firefighting and prevention services in order to protect life, property and natural resources from damage by fire; • Control persons and premises engaged in manufacturing, preparations, storage handling, sale or distribution of food or drink including intoxicating substances; • Prohibit and control the use of land and erection of buildings in the interest of public health, safely and orderly development of the Council area; • Demolish or remove buildings which are a danger to public health or safety and do not conform to plans and specifications approved by the Councils; • Establish and maintain public amenities such as parks, zoos, gardens, pleasure grounds, camping grounds, caravan sites and an open spaces; • Establish and maintain hospitals, clinics, health centers and environmental and health services; and • Establish and maintain cemeteries, crematoria, and mortuaries and provide for the burial of the dead and destitute persons who die in the area of the Council. HAVE THE COUNCILS AROUND THE COUNTRY THE CAPABILITIES TO TAKE WHAT IS EXPECTED AFTER THE DEVOLUTION? (i) Local Councils are already doing tremendous work in the provision of public services and enhancing social and economic development to the local communities in the respective district boundaries. (ii) Levels of capabilities differ from one Council to another owing to different levels of development and status. The financial strength of the Lusaka City Council cannot be compared to that of a small district like say Kafue, or Chongwe. (iii) Provision of services largely depends on the balance of Estimates of Income over expenditure, meaning that each Council can only spend as much as it earns in terms of service delivery. (iv) The Decentralization Policy assures that Local communities will be empowered by devolving decision making authority, functions and matching resources from the centre to the lowest level in order to improve efficient and effectiveness in the delivery of services. HOW MUCH RESOURCES ARE ACCESSED BY LOCAL COUNCILS? (i) This depends on sources of income for each Council, and the type. (ii) Some smaller Council have a smaller annual budget of say K2.2 billion, which is far below a monthly salary wage bill for Lusaka City Council. (iii) District Councils, in addition to their local resources, receive annual grants from the centre to fund capital projects. Bigger Councils (Cities) are encouraged to generate own income from local sources of income such as property rates. title: Who we are – Mbala Municipal Council
text_content: Who we are – Mbala Municipal Council Menu MBALA DISTRICT NORTHERN PROVINCE - ZAMBIA OUR VISION The vision of the district is a prosperous district through provision of improved equitable, quality and diversified Municipal Services in an effective and efficient manner in order to enhance sustainable development. OUR MISSION Our mission is to “accelerate development efforts towards the vision 2030 without leaving anyone behind.” About The District Mbala District is situated in the Northern Province of the Republic of Zambia. It shares international boundaries with the Republic of Tanzania in the north, and district boundaries with Senga in the southeast, Nakonde in the east, Kasama in the south and Mpulungu in the west. The district has a surface area of about 10,832 Km2 . Mbala district has an altitude ranging from 400m above sea level in the western side where the Great Rift Valley lies and 2,067m above sea level in the South-eastern side where Nsunzu Mountain is, the highest mountain peak in the district. Temperatures range from 15o C in the cold season to 29o C in the hot season. On average, the district receives 1,200 mm of rainfall annually which is good for agriculture. Mbala District has 9 wards: Nsunzu, Lwandi, Kawimbe, Mwamba, Mwambezi, Kazimolwa, Moto Moto, Intala and Kalambo Ward. Tourist Attractions The Kalambo Falls The Kalambo Falls, Zambia’s tallest water falls standing at 235 metres tall is a single drop water fall located on the boarder of Zambia and Tanzania at the South East end of Lake Tanganyika. Downstream of the falls is the gorge with a width of about 1km and a depth of 300 meters. In 2023, archaeologists announced the discovery of wooden structures estimated to be 476,000 years old predating Homo Sapiens, making the Kalambo Falls one of the most important archaeological sites in Africa. The MotoMoto Museum Motomoto Museum located 4.2km Northeast of Mbala Town is the second largest Museum in Zambia after Livingstone Museum, furnished with a magnificent display of ethnography and cultural artifacts. It was officially opened in 1974 and named after Bishop Joseph Dupont a pioneer missionary who was nicknamed “Moto Moto” meaning fire in Swahili language. The Museum houses collections of weapons of World War I, earliest tools used by mankind, Slavery, Trade and Natural History artifacts. Investment Opportunities - Agriculture History The facility began as Tanganyika Airport in 1885 and later became known as Abercorn International Airport during the colonial period. After Zambia’s independence, it became Mbala International Airport. In the mid-1970s, it was converted mainly into a Zambia Air Force (ZAF) military facility. In 1986, it was named Samora Machel in honour of Mozambican President Samora Machel. Samora Machel’s last journey is closely linked to Mbala: he departed from the area in October 1986 before his aircraft crashed at Mbuzini, South Africa, killing him and others. The Mbala Cenotaph, also called the Mbala War Memorial or Abercorn Memorial, is an important historical monument connected with World War I. It stands at the main roundabout in Mbala, formerly known as Abercorn. It commemorates 1,467 men from Northern Rhodesia who served as carriers for the British forces during World War I and died from fighting, wounds or sickness. It particularly remembers 433 African carriers who died in Northern Rhodesia during the war. Mbala was the location of the formal surrender of the German forces in East Africa on 25 November 1918, bringing the East African campaign of World War I to an end. title: CDF UPGRADES MBULU MARKET WITH A MODERN MARKET SHELTER
text_content: Significant progress has been made in the construction of Mbulu Modern Market Shelter, a key project in Mbala, funded under the 2024 and 2025 Constituency Development Fund (CDF) allocations. With a total project cost of 6.8 million Kwacha, the project was flagged off on 30 th December 2025 and is set to enhance local commerce in the District. With the Substructure erected and Roofing installed, the contractor is currently laying the concrete slab which will form the foundation of the 36.4m x 30m Market Shelter, representing 65% progress towards completion. The Market Shelter will also feature 260 Lockable Storage Stands for Marketeers seeking to secure goods overnight. Furthermore, Security Lights will be installed to enhance safety and extend trading hours within the facility. As part of the project scope, a 10,000 Litre capacity Water Reticulation System has been successfully installed, ensuring that the market will have reliable water supply for vendors and patrons. Mbulu Market is recognized as the biggest market in Mbala with a population of over 1000 people, serving as a vital economic hub for the District. The modernization of this market facility will provide a safer, secure and dignified trading space, envisioned to ultimately boost local commerce and economic growth in the District.

title: Overview – Mbala Municipal Council
text_content: Overview – Mbala Municipal Council Menu CDF OVERVIEW The Constituency Development Fund (CDF) continues to redefine governance in Zambia. In the 2026 Budget, allocations have risen to K40 million per constituency from the K1.6 million in 2021, bringing the national total to K6.245 billion. The CDF is not simply a funding source; it represents decentralisation and community-driven development. Citizens directly shape their priorities, whether in classrooms, health facilities, bridges, or youth enterprises. The President has prioritised CDF because it delivers tangible outcomes that citizens can see and feel. Evidence-led implementation is central to this priority. The Presidential Delivery Unit is working with the Ministry of Local Government and Rural Development to strengthen impact measurement, enhance citizen engagement, and deploy digital systems for CDF management and reporting. The goal is to ensure transparency, accountability, and timely delivery. Already, thousands of projects have been funded since the CDF’s expansion. But success depends on partnerships. Local authorities must improve oversight, civil society should support monitoring, and communities must take ownership of projects. The private sector also has a role in co-financing youth skills training and community infrastructure. By linking CDF to the President’s vision of inclusive growth and equity, Zambia is building a governance model that empowers citizens, strengthens service delivery, and ensures that development is achieved constituency by constituency. With improved systems and accountability, the CDF is becoming a symbol of responsive governance. title: CITIZENS’ VERSION IDPs INTRODUCED
text_content: The Ministry of Local Government and Rural Development has embarked on the development of Citizen’s Version Integrated Development Plans (IDPs) in all 116 districts across the nation. The Integrated Development Plan is a comprehensive document which captures critical information on developmental programmes to be implemented in the district over a period of ten years, subject to review every five years. As a critical process in the development of Citizen’s Version Integrated Development Plans, the Ministry of Local Government and Rural Development, in collaboration with UNICEF and the Policy Monitoring and Research Centre, undertook Backstopping and Finalization Workshops in provincial centres across the country to ensure the development of quality Citizen’s Version IDPs. Speaking during the official opening of the Northern and Luapula Province Backstopping and Orientation Workshop held from 15th to 22nd September 2025 at Teja Executive Lodge in Mansa, Deputy Permanent Secretary for Luapula Province, Mr. Evans Sikabbubba stated that, the Integrated Development Plan is a critical tool in the decentralization process as it provides a coherent participatory and evidence based frame work, for guiding development in our districts over a medium and long term period. “Citizen’s Version IDPs are particularly important because they make the IDP accessible and understandable, to all stakeholders especially community members who are the core beneficiaries of development initiatives. Simplifying and translating the technical details of the IDPs into a format that the public can easily engage with will foster citizen participation, inclusivity and accountability in our planning and implementing processes,” he stated. The Deputy Permanent Secretary further reiterated that the development of Citizen’s Version IDPs demonstrates Government’s commitment to ensuring that all provinces are fully engaged in planning processes, thereby strengthening citizen participation, accountability and inclusive development across the country. During the Workshops, Local Authorities submitted their completed draft Citizen’s Version IDPs for finalization after which approval, distribution and sensitization to the general public will follow. In attendance was the Director of Physical Planning from the Ministry of Local Government and Rural Development, representatives of the Provincial Local Government Officers for Northern and Luapula Provinces, Provincial Planners, UNICEF, Principals and various key officers from Local Authorities in Northern and Luapula Provinces. title: MBALA CDF AMBULANCE COMMISSIONED
text_content: Mbala Member of Parliament and Minister for Muchinga Province, Hon. Njavwa Simutowe has commissioned the newly procured Ambulance which was delivered to Mbala Constituency on Saturday 20th September 2025. This follows the recent flag-off of the first 119 CDF procured Ambulances by the Minister of Local Government and Rural Development, which took place in Lusaka on 17th September 2025. Speaking during the handover ceremony held on 22nd September 2025 at the Civic Centre in Mbala, Hon. Simutowe thanked the President of the Republic of Zambia Mr. Hakainde Hichilema for the initiative to purchase Ambulances for all Constituencies in the country under CDF. “Zambia is vast and all of us were looking to Central Government to provide what we needed. But with the coming of the increased scope of CDF, rural areas like Mbala which were lagging behind in terms of development now have a different story through the transformation being implemented in the Education, Health, Public Infrastructure and Social Economic sectors,” he said. He stated that, through CDF Mbala Constituency now has an Ambulance, a Monitoring Vehicle, a Police Vehicle, a Grader, Tipper Truck and a Tractor Loader Backhoe. He also disclosed that CDF has additionally empowered the Mbala Community through Empowerment Funds and sent children to go and learn different professional skills. And Mbala District Commissioner, Mr. Jestus Sikazwe has urged the District Health Office to ensure that proper care and maintenance of the Ambulance is upheld to prolong its lifespan to help the people of Mbala for many years to come. The Minister also took the opportunity to commend Mbala Municipal Council management for patching all portholes in the Central Business District and encouraged them to continue the hard work. Hon. title: DRAFT AMENDMENTS TO THE CONSTITUTION SUBMITTED
text_content: Following the appointment of the Technical Committee on Drafting Amendments to the Constitution of Zambia, by His Excellency President Hakainde Hichilema, Mbala District joined the Northern Province Virtual Public Sitting to make submissions to the Committee. The purpose of the Committee was to consult the people of Zambia to review and benchmark best constitutional practices, propose amendments to the Constitution with a view to consolidate democracy and constitutionalism, enhance equitable and balanced representation and promote inclusivity, accountability and effective representation in governance. The Committee commenced public consultations and receiving of submissions through public sittings held at Provincial headquarters while virtual sittings for districts took place at Civic Centres. Led by the District Commissioner, His Worship the Mayor and Town Clerk, various stakeholders gathered at Mbala Municipal Council Chamber on 30th October 2025 and made submissions through the Mambwe Royal Establishment Spokesperson, Mr. Christopher Mengo Siame who submitted that; – There is need for clear guidance on the delimitation of Wards and Constituencies, as some areas such as Nonde Ward are experiencing boundary overlaps between Mbala and Mpulungu Districts. – Leadership should not be restricted by academic qualification. Rather being a Zambian Citizen should be the main qualification for one to serve in any public office. – The Grade Twelve Certificate requirement for one to run for public office be removed. – By-Elections be abolished and Ministers be appointed outside of Parliament. – Petitions for Members of Parliament and Councillors be resolved within 21 working days while Presidential petitions should be resolved within 14 working days to enhance efficiency and fairness in governance. And Team Leader for the Constitution Amendment Programme Mr. Robbinson Chongo called on Zambians to actively participate in the constitutional review process to promote good governance and sustainable national development. title: MBALA STAKEHOLDERS WELCOME THE CONSTRUCTION OF A TRUCK PARK
text_content: Stakeholders have welcomed the move to construct a Truck Park at the Mbala – Mpulungu Junction in Mbala District. Speaking during a Stakeholder Meeting held on 02nd July 2025 at Mbala – Mpulungu Junction, Mbala Municipal Council Town Clerk Mrs. Laura Yumba Munkanta guided the stakeholders to consider the benefits of constructing a Truck Park at the strategic location, including traffic decongestion, job creation, economic growth, revenue for the Local Authority and the provision of a conducive, secure parking area for truckers, with water and sanitation facilities. The Truck Park will further be constructed with a number of shops which will be rented out to local traders to provide goods and services to truckers and patrons of the facility. Mrs. Munkanta also guided the stakeholders to consider the environmental as well as social impacts the facility may pose and devise ways to mitigate them before the commencement of the project. She further presented the sources of funding, budget line, future expansion and upgrade plans, as well as the need for continued collaboration with stakeholders to ensure harmonization of objectives and expectations. Stakeholders present unanimously supported the venture and requested the Council to commence and complete the project timely, as they foresee development with numerous benefits to the District. The stakeholders further suggested that a steering committee of stakeholders be formed to assist the Council supervise and direct works when the project commences. Meanwhile, differently abled stakeholders requested that Persons Living With Disabilities be considered during the allocation of the shops to support their efforts in sustaining their families.

title: PROVINCIAL MINISTER HON. LEONARD MBAO HANDS OVER K3.7 MILLION IN CDF EMPOWERMENT LOANS TO MBALA BENEFICIARIES
text_content: Provincial Minister for Northern Province, Hon. Leonard Mbao, has handed over Constituency Development Fund Empowerment Loans to 28 enterprises in Mbala Constituency, amounting to a total of K3,736,935.61 under the 2025 CDF allocation, during a Handover Ceremony held today, at the Civic Centre. During his speech, Hon. Mbao stated that from 2022 to date, Mbala Municipal Council has disbursed CDF Empowerment Loans to 127 beneficiaries across the nine Wards of the Constituency, amounting to a total of K12,609,425. The Minister reminded beneficiaries to adhere to the CDF guidelines in the management and repayment of their Empowerment Loans and appealed to the CDF Committee to consider more Women, Youths and Persons Living With Disabilities, during the approval of applications for CDF Empowerment Funds. “in the last four years, the Constituency Development Fund Community Projects, Empowerment Funds, Bursaries and Presidential Directives have led the nation towards an upward trajectory, through the CDF’s holistic approach implemented by the UPND Government” he said. Meanwhile, Mbala District Commissioner, Mr. Jestus Sikazwe challenged beneficiaries of CDF Empowerment Funds to be proud ambassadors, giving testament to the feasible transformative power of the Constituency Development Fund after having benefitted from it. And Town Clerk for Mbala Municipal Council, Mrs. Laura Yumba Munkanta revealed that the Council has previously disbursed CDF Empowerment Grants to 502 cooperatives in the last four years. She further stated that 688 students have been sponsored under the Skills Development Bursary and 471 pupils under the Secondary Boarding School Bursary.

title: A COMMUNITY VISION REALISED THROUGH CDF – KAKUNGU DAY SECONDARY SCHOOL COMMISSIONED
text_content: Residents, Teachers and Pupils of Kakungu Village in Lwandi Ward Mbala, gathered today to witness the ground breaking ceremony during which Northern Province Minister, Hon. Leonard Mbao commissioned Kakungu Day Secondary School, comprised of a 1×4 Classroom Block completed under the Constituency Development Fund. In the recent past, Kakungu Primary School catered for both the primary and secondary streams overwhelming both the educators and learners. Out of pure determination, the catchment community came together and begun the construction of the secondary school to decongest the primary school. However, due to lack of resources and capacity, the community was unable to complete the building. But today, Kakungu Secondary School is a functional facility thanks to the intervention of the Constituency Development Fund. Speaking during the Handover Ceremony held today at the school, Hon. Leonard Mbao stated that the project was implemented at a cost of K598,203.60, and furnished with 100 desks procured through CDF, fulfilling the Presidential Directive that no child should sit on the floor. And Head Teacher Mr. Mwila Mutelelwe revealed that the addition of a secondary school has decongested the primary school and created room for the influx of children who have enrolled since the introduction of the free education policy. He further stated that the newly commissioned secondary school has attracted pupils from several villages serving as the only secondary school in the vicinity. In her remarks, District Education Board Secretary Mrs. Juanita Mulenga confirmed that the school will go a long way in ensuring that every child in the surrounding communities will have access to secondary education. She further thanked the government for supporting the construction of the Classroom Block through CDF as it has presented a conducive environment to provide effective teaching and learning which will change generations in the community. And in her vote of thanks, Linda Shumba Head Girl of the school recalled how access to a conducive learning environment was but a dream, now realised. She expressed gratitude on behalf of her fellow pupils, to the President of the Republic of Zambia, Mr. Hakainde Hichilema for enhancing access to education through the Constituency Development Fund.

title: MBALA MUNICIPAL COUNCIL DISBURSES OVER FIVE MILLION KWACHA IN CDF EMPOWERMENT GRANTS AND LOANS
text_content: Mbala Municipal Council has handed over Constituency Development Fund Empowerment Loans to 33 applicants, amounting to K3,417,000 , and K2,283,000 to 151 Grant beneficiaries across the 9 Wards of Mbala Constituency. This brings the total amount disbursed in the 2024 Women, Youth and Community Empowerment Fund to K5,700,000, indicating an increase by K323,000 in comparison to K5,377.000 approved in 2023. Speaking during the Handover Ceremony held on 17th July, 2024 at the Civic Centre, District Commissioner Jestus Sikazwe who graced the Ceremony as Guest of Honor commended the Government of his Excellency President Hakainde Hichilema, who has committed himself to practically address challenges faced by vulnerable communities through the consistent disbursement of the Constituency Development Fund (CDF). The District Commissioner stated that, successful implementation of Empowerment Funds among 2022 and 2023 beneficiaries has demonstrated the undeniable transforming power of CDF in the District, as observed during the monitoring activities conducted by the Council in collaboration with Local Leaders. “Through CDF, communities are making strides to gain resilience to effects of climate change, poverty and lack of employment.” And Town Clerk for Mbala Municipal Council Mrs. Laura Yumba Munkanta commended the outgoing CDF Committee, the Local Authority and Access Bank for the timely processing and disbursement of CDF Empowerment Funds to the beneficiaries. She however appealed to beneficiaries to be available during monitoring visits and to correctly utilize their Empowerment Funds or risk being held accountable through the laid down CDF Guidelines. And in his Vote of Thanks, Reverend Silondwa, Chairman of the Pastors Fellowship Savings Group, as a beneficiary of 2024 Empowerment Grants, expressed gratitude to the Government for considering his group under CDF thereby acknowledging that the clergy is part and parcel of the common challenges being faced in the nation such as climate change and poverty. Beneficiaries who previously received Financial Literacy, were further sensitized during the Ceremony to ensure that their funds go through the bank frequently and before any business transaction is made, in order to build financial statements and efficient record keeping. Meanwhile, William Sinkamba, a local entrepreneur gave testament to the growth he has experienced in his business through the CDF Empowerment Loan he received under the 2023 allocation.

title: MBALA MUNICIPAL COUNCIL CONSTRUCTS NEW ABLUTION BLOCK AT MBULU MARKET
text_content: Mbala Municipal Council has commissioned a newly constructed Ablution Block at Mbulu Market worth K311,000 using the capital component of the Local Government Equalization Fund. The Ablution Block is fitted with 6 toilets and 4 hand washing sinks in the ladies section and 6 toilets, 4 hand washing sinks and 4 urinals in the gents section. Prior to the construction of the new Ablution Block, marketeers and patrons of Mbulu Market were restricted to using an old Ablution Block with only 1 female and 1 male toilet which were in a deplorable state. The Local Authority gave priority to the construction of the new Ablution Block as Mbulu market is the biggest and most populated market in the District but had inadequate toilets which could not accommodate the masses. Speaking during the commissioning ceremony held on Thursday 23 rd November 2023, His Worship the Mayor Mr. Mulenga Sinyangwe commended the Local Authority for accommodating the construction of the Ablution Block under Capital Funds in order to bring dignity, proper sanitation and prevent disease outbreaks. The Mayor also commended the contractor for delivering quality works on the project. In his vote of thanks, the Market Committee Chairperson expressed gratitude to the Local Authority and to Civic leaders for replacing the old Ablution Block which they have used for decades.

title: MBALA MUNICIPAL COUNCIL LAUNCHES CHILDREN’S CORNER AT TVMI LIBRARY
text_content: Mbala Municipal Council has today launched the Children’s Corner in an event held at TVMI Library. The Children’s Corner is a newly introduced section of the library, furnished and stocked to cater to the reading, research, and learning needs of children between the ages of 1 to 15 years old. Out of its mandate to provide access to information, knowledge, and educational resources, the Local Authority has been actively engaging well-wishers to revamp the library and finally managed to secure a donation of K29,459.00, 3000 books and Staff Training from Book Aid International in partnership with the Zambia Library Service, which has enabled the establishment of the Children’s Corner. Speaking during the launch, Town Clerk for Mbala Municipal Council Mrs. Laura Yumba Munkanta expressed excitement at the new addition to the facility, as it will contribute to the establishment of a solid literacy foundation for children at their critical learning age. She further expressed gratitude to Book Aid International and the Zambia Library Service for funding the establishment of the Children’s Corner, the first of its kind in the District. And Mbala District Education Board Secretary in his remarks urged parents and teachers to encourage learners to utilize the Children’s Corner in order to promote the culture of reading among children as it is crucial to education. He further encouraged learners to subscribe for membership so as to fully benefit from the services being provided at the facility. The launch was characterized by a spelling competition between Grade 6 students from Chila Primary School and Mbala Primary School. Mbala Primary School walked away with the winning prize inclusive of hardcover books, pencils, and pens. In attendance was Mbala Municipal Council Town Clerk, District Education Board Secretary, Constituency Development Fund Committee Chairperson, Local Authority Management, various Stakeholders, Teachers and Pupils from various schools. The facility shall be accessible free of charge, but attracts a membership fee of K10 per month or K100 per year, for access to services such as borrowing books.

title: ZAMBIA CELEBRATES 59 YEARS OF INDEPENDENCE
text_content: Mbala District joined the rest of the nation in the celebration of 59 years of Zambia’s independence. Government Departments, Parastatals, the Zambia Air Force, Civil Society Organizations, and Citizens from all walks of life joined the procession of the march past from the Cenotaph to the Civic Centre, where the commemoration was held on October 24 th 2023. Speaking during the event, District Commissioner Mrs. Anne Paul encouraged Zambians to sustain the freedom, peace and unity which freedom fighters shed their blood for in the fight for Zambia’s independence from colonization and slavery. She encouraged all to emulate the valor and courage exhibited by the freedom fighters even to the point of d eath. The commemoration was also graced by the presence of Mr. Blackson Chinama, a freedom fighter who took part in Zambia’s fight for freedom in 1964. In his speech, Mr. Chinama encouraged Zambians to continue the fight for freedom from issues that have affected the average Zambian such as poverty. The assembly honored the senior citizen with a round of applause for contributing to the attainment of mother Zambia’s freedom. And in her welcoming remarks, Town Clerk for Mbala Municipal Council, Mrs. Laura Yumba Munkanta stated that, it was her privilege to be part of the independence celebration as it is the day when our forefathers won the fight for the freedom we enjoy today. Mbala District also observed the hosting of the flag and gun salute on the night of Independence Eve at the Civic Centre.

title: MBALA MUNICIPAL COUNCIL AWARDS CDF EMPOWERMENT LOANS TO 22 BENEFICIARY GROUPS
text_content: Luapula Province Minister & Member of Parliament for Mbala Constituency, Honorable Njavwa Simutowe has today awarded CDF Empowerment Loans to 22 approved beneficiaries from the 2022 CDF allocation and 1 approved beneficiary from the 2023 allocation. The 22 approved beneficiaries who have been awarded under the 2022 CDF allocation are a fraction of beneficiaries who will also be awarded within the next few weeks under the 2022 allocation collectively amounting to K2,229,290. Speaking during the awarding ceremony held today at the civic centre, the honorable minister expressed gratification to witness the empowerment of small and medium scale enterprises (SME’s), Cooperatives, Clubs, Associations and individuals with loans that will enable them to initiate or boost already existing businesses, which will result in job creation and economic growth in the District. And in her welcoming remarks, Town Clerk for Mbala Municipal Council Mrs. Laura Yumba Munkanta assured civic leaders and stakeholders that the Local Authority is committed to providing guidance to the beneficiaries and monitoring their progress to ensure that CDF guidelines are strictly adhered to in order to maximize the output of the businesses that the beneficiaries will take on. The Town Clerk further urged the banks to expedite the processing and issuing of CDF empowerment loans to avoid unnecessary delays. Mrs. Munkanta also stated that the approved beneficiaries underwent financial literacy training on 29th September 2023 and is therefore confident that the beneficiaries are well aware of the terms and conditions of the CDF loans they have received and will therefore abide by them. And in her remarks, District Commissioner Mrs. Anne Paul challenged beneficiaries of CDF empowerment loans and grants to bring forth testament of the actualization of CDF in order to build the faith of the public in the government’s efforts, especially to those who have not received empowerment funds yet. Meanwhile his Worship the Mayor Mr. Mulenga Sinyangwe urged the beneficiaries to refrain from diverting the funds to endeavors contrary to what was submitted in their applications as this will attract repercussions.

title: PROVINCIAL MINISTER NJAVWA SIMUTOWE – MP HANDS OVER GRADER TO COUNCIL PURCHASED THROUGH CDF.
text_content: Mbala Municipal Council has procured a brand new Grader through the 2023 Constituency Development Fund at a cost of K2,499,500. The Grader was commissioned by Honorable Njavwa Simutowe – MP during a ceremony held on 18 th August 2023 at Old Location Round About, in the presence of His Worship The Mayor Mr. Mulenga Sinyangwe, the District Commissioner Mrs. Anne Paul, government departments, stakeholders, community members and the press. The acquisition of the new Grader has enabled the Local Authority to begin rehabilitating feeder roads thereby improving rural road connectivity and bring about inclusive socio economic transformation in the District. The law maker in his speech highlighted challenges faced by Government Officers such as difficulty in reaching rural areas to deliver public services due to the dilapidated and impassable roads the District is characterized by. This has also posed a challenge for patients to easily access Health Centres and farmers to transport their produce to the intended market. Honorable Simutowe has further commended the Local Authority for beginning the procurement process of a Tipper Truck, an  accompanying piece of machinery required in the rehabilitation of feeder roads. Speaking during the event, the District Commissioner Mrs. Anne Paul urged the Local Authority and the CDF Committee to plan for the procurement of complimenting equipment such as a roller compactor, and other requisite equipment in order to complete the set as the Grader cannot be used in isolation. And Ward Councilor for Kazimolwa Ward, Hon. Hastings Sinyangwe in his vote of thanks commended the government for strengthening the capacity of Local Authorities through massive increment in the constituency development fund allocations.

title: MBALA DISBURSES OVER K2 MILLION IN CDF EMPOWERMENT GRANTS
text_content: Mbala Municipal Council disbursed K2,151,856,55 in Grants under the Women, Youth and Community Empowerment component of the 2023 CDF allocation during an awarding ceremony held on 23 rd June 2023 at the Civic Centre. 76 groups including Cooperatives, Clubs, and Youth Groups drawn from all the nine wards of Mbala District received Constituency Development Fund Grants during the well-attended ceremony. Applications which were funded include piggery, poultry, peanut butter processing, sunflower oil processing, fish farming, goat rearing, village banking and crop growing among others. Speaking during the event, Hon.Simutowe reminded beneficiaries of the government’s expectation that the disbursed grants must be used  to to implement the viable projects applied for, in order to relieve the burden of poverty in the communities, uplift the wellbeing of the people and stimulate economic activities in respective wards. He further encouraged the beneficiaries to maximize output from their ventures so as to bring sustenance in their livelihoods, create jobs and contribute meaningfully to the national food basket. Meanwhile, Mbala Municipal Council Town Clerk, Mrs. Laura Yumba Munkanta stated that the Local Authority had previously given out grants to 48 groups and bursaries to 79 learners under the 2022 CDF allocation and encouraged community members to continue submitting applications as the submission and processing of applications is an ongoing process. The awarding ceremony was graced by Hon. Njavwa Simutowe in the company of The District Commissioner Mrs. Anne Paul, Deputy Mayor Mr. Alfred Ntuntu, the District Commissioner Mrs. Anne Paul and the Town Clerk Mrs. Laura Yumba Munkanta. Also in attendance was the CDF Committee, and representatives of Cooperatives, Clubs and groups across all wards of the District.
